Now That There Are 4 Taylor's Version Albums, I Had To Find The Most Different And The Most Similar Tracks
==========================================================================================================

It's a new soundtrack, I could dance to this beat!

[![Image 1: Andrew Firriolo](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/user_images/KXQBGdOMr_large.jpg?crop=499:500;0,284&downsize=120:*&output-format=jpg&output-quality=auto) by Andrew FirrioloBuzzFeed Staff](https://www.buzzfeed.com/andrewfirriolo)

[![Image 2: BuzzFeed Community Team](https://img.buzzfeed.com/store-an-image-prod-us-east-1/p9aVli648.png?downsize=120:*&output-format=jpg&output-quality=auto) Approved and edited by BuzzFeed Community Team](https://www.buzzfeed.com/community/about)

*   [](https://bsky.app/intent/compose?text=Now%20That%20There%20Are%204%20Taylor%27s%20Version%20Albums%2C%20I%20Had%20To%20Find%20The%20Most%20Different%20And%20The%20Most%20Similar%20Tracks%0A%0Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fwww.buzzfeed.com%2Fandrewfirriolo%2Fcomparing-taylors-version-original-albums%3Futm_source%3Ddynamic%26utm_campaign%3Dbfsharebluesky)
    
*   [](https://www.facebook.com/dialog/share?href=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.buzzfeed.com%2Fandrewfirriolo%2Fcomparing-taylors-version-original-albums%3Futm_source%3Ddynamic%26utm_campaign%3Dbfsharefacebook&app_id=45075597673)
    
*   [](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.buzzfeed.com%2Fandrewfirriolo%2Fcomparing-taylors-version-original-albums%3Futm_source%3Ddynamic%26utm_campaign%3Dbfsharepinterest&description=Now%20That%20There%20Are%204%20Taylor%27s%20Version%20Albums%2C%20I%20Had%20To%20Find%20The%20Most%20Different%20And%20The%20Most%20Similar%20Tracks&media=https%3A%2F%2Fimg-mkr.buzzfeed.com%2Fbuzzfeed-static%2Fstatic%2F2023-10%2F30%2F15%2Fenhanced%2Fa0ebca250978%2Foriginal-924-1698681170-2.jpg%3Fcrop%3D2996%3A1997%3B0%2C0%26resize%3D1250%3A830%3Ftemplate%3Dpinterest-vertical-dots-v1%26title%3DTm93IFRoYXQgVGhlcmUgQXJlIDQgVGF5bG9yJ3MgVmVyc2lvbiBBbGJ1bXMsIEkgSGFkIFRvIEZpbmQgVGhlIE1vc3QgRGlmZmVyZW50IEFuZCBUaGUgTW9zdCBTaW1pbGFyIFRyYWNrcw%3D%3D%26color1%3Dblack)
    
*   

Hi, I'm Andrew, a senior data analyst for BuzzFeed and a [Swiftie](https://www.buzzfeed.com/evelinamedina/taylor-swift-trivia)! As each Taylor’s Version is released, (now updated for _1989_), I thought it would be fun to investigate: _which Taylor's Versions sound the closest and the most different to their first versions?\*_
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  ![Image 3: 1989 (Taylor's Version) Album Cover](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-10/30/13/asset/f1e45e03753b/sub-buzz-546-1698674374-1.jpg?downsize=700%3A%2A&output-quality=auto&output-format=auto)

Republic Records

_\*This analysis focuses on high-level audio characteristics, so lyric changes (like in "Better Than Revenge") won't affect the results._

Where does the data come from?
------------------------------

The Spotify API holds [descriptive audio characteristics](https://developer.spotify.com/documentation/web-api/reference/#/operations/get-audio-features)\* for songs. I gathered this data for every Taylor's Version and its first version on the deluxe editions: 20 songs from _Fearless_ (I'm considering "If This Was A Movie" to be a _Fearless_ song), 20 from _Red_, 16 from _Speak Now,_ and 16 from _1989_.

The variables I chose are:

**1) Acousticness:** a measure between 0 and 1 of how "acoustic" a track is. The closer to 1, the more acoustic.

**2) Danceability:** a measure between 0 and 1 of how well the track can be used for dancing (closer to 1 means more danceable). It takes into account metrics like tempo and rhythm.

**3) Energy:** a measure between 0 and 1 of intensity within a track ("energetic tracks feel fast, loud, and noisy"). A higher score means a higher energy.

**4) Instrumentalness:** a measure between 0 and 1 of whether a track is instrumental. A measure closer to 1 is a higher likelihood of no vocals.

**5) Speechness:** a measure between 0 and 1 detecting spoken word within a track. The higher the measure, the higher the probability that the track is spoken word.

**6) Valence:** a measure between 0 and 1 describing the "musical positiveness" of a track (0: most sad vs. 1: most happy-sounding).

**7) Loudness:** The overall loudness of a track, in decibels.

Every variable in the data set ranges between 0 and 1, except for loudness. To make sure every variable was on the same scale, I normalized the loudness over each pair of albums to range between 0 and 1.

I chose to exclude metrics like liveness, which detects the presence of an audience within a track (none of the songs were recorded live), and things like tempo, key, and time signature which remain consistent between both versions.

_(See link above for the full definitions of the variables)._

The methodology:
----------------

  ![Image 4: photo of Taylor Swift from Jimmy Fallon's Ew segment with the distance formula overlayed on top](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-07/13/15/asset/591f796724af/sub-buzz-852-1689263684-1.jpg?downsize=700%3A%2A&output-quality=auto&output-format=auto)

NBC/BuzzFeed

For each pair of songs, I calculated a distance score using the above formula (though with 7 dimensions instead of 2).

The final result was 72 distances, which I ranked highest to lowest.

Here's the 20 pairs (Taylor's Version vs. first version) that are the most different from each other:
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

_For each song, I generated a graph showing the audio metrics for Taylor's Version and its first version. If a variable on the graph only shows one album cover, it is because the values are so similar that the points overlapped._

20 — "Speak Now"
----------------

![Image 6: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-07/9/15/asset/d2e07cde1d15/sub-buzz-3228-1688915237-1.jpg)

Scott Legato/TAS23 / Getty Images for TAS Rights Management/Big Machine Records/Republic Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.228

**Taylor's Version's biggest difference:** higher acousticness

I always wanted a music video for this song (hint hint, Taylor if you're reading this)! From the opening chords of Taylor's Version, the acoustic guitar sounds more prominent, and the overall track feels less produced than the first version. The data reflects this, with Taylor's Version receiving a higher acousticness score.

19 — "Never Grow Up"
--------------------

![Image 8: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-07/9/15/asset/35882d57811f/sub-buzz-3461-1688915250-1.jpg)

Scott Legato/TAS23 / Getty Images for TAS Rights Management/Big Machine Records/Republic Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.234

**Taylor's Version's biggest difference:** higher loudness

This song has always been a tearjerker, and Taylor's Version is no exception. Taylor's Version is a louder song, which I especially heard in the choruses.

18 — "Mean"
-----------

![Image 10: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-07/9/15/asset/ddccda2938a1/sub-buzz-5077-1688915264-1.jpg)

Scott Legato/TAS23 / Getty Images for TAS Rights Management/Big Machine Records/Republic Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.235

**Taylor's Version's biggest difference:** lower valence (less happiness)

One pattern I've seen in the data is the difficulty to recreate similar valence ("musical positiveness") when the first version has a very high score (0.789 out of 1). You'll see this concept also apply to songs further down the ranking.

From an instrumental standpoint, some of the higher frequencies (mainly the banjo in the chorus) sound more noticeable in the first version and a bit lower in the mix in Taylor's Version.

17 — "You Are In Love"
----------------------

![Image 12: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-10/30/14/asset/ba956eda8a88/sub-buzz-1277-1698674816-3.jpg?crop=1600:1388;0,104)

Republic Records/Big Machine Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.237

**Taylor's Version's biggest difference:** higher valence (more happiness)

This song is SO underrated, and is one of my favorite tracks from _1989_. Taylor’s vocals shine in Taylor’s Version, sounding more ambient and light. An example is the first line of the last chorus, “you can hear it in the silence."

16 — "Forever & Always (Piano Version)"
---------------------------------------

![Image 14: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-07/9/15/asset/1007dd4722e1/sub-buzz-3526-1688915285-5.jpg)

Republic Records/Big Machine Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.242

**Taylor's Version's biggest difference:** higher loudness

I've always thought "Forever & Always (Piano Version)" was so clever, because the non-piano version sounds like a _completely_ different song. It's amazing how the same lyrics can be felt so differently.

In Taylor's Version, the piano used in the recording sounds deeper and the vocals are louder.

15 — "Last Kiss"
----------------

![Image 16: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-07/9/15/asset/35882d57811f/sub-buzz-3461-1688915308-3.jpg)

Scott Legato/TAS23 / Getty Images for TAS Rights Management/Big Machine Records/Republic Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.259

**Taylor's Version's biggest difference:** higher danceability

The irony that I'm writing this on July 9th! As expected, the valence (happiness) is low in both versions, with Taylor stating that "Last Kiss" is the saddest song she's ever written.

Taylor's Version has a lower acousticness score and higher danceability than the first version. The piano and bass-heavy drums are louder on Taylor's Version, especially in the first verse.

14 — "Style"
------------

![Image 18: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-10/30/14/asset/291411aa44ca/sub-buzz-605-1698674960-1.jpg?crop=1600:1376;0,108)

Republic Records/Big Machine Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.259

**Taylor's Version's biggest difference:** lower valence (less happiness)

The two audio qualities setting “Style (Taylor’s Version)” and “Style” apart are valence and loudness. Taylor’s Version amps up the volume, especially the vocals and synths in the chorus, while the first version feels more blended.

“Style (Taylor’s Version)” has the highest loudness score on _1989 (Taylor’s Version)_, whereas “Style” only received the sixth highest loudness score on _1989_. This is likely the reason for the decreased valence (lower “musical positiveness”) in Taylor’s Version.

13 — "Clean"
------------

![Image 20: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-10/30/14/asset/242d0eff2713/sub-buzz-598-1698675130-1.jpg?crop=1600:1392;0,100)

Republic Records/Big Machine Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.259

**Taylor's Version's biggest difference:** lower loudness

In contrast to “Style," “Clean (Taylor’s Version)” has a lower loudness than the first version. Taylor’s Version has a more gentle feel, perhaps from singing the lyrics from a new perspective. Imogen Heap’s backing vocals also sound more crisp and clear in the last chorus.

12 — "Out of the Woods"
-----------------------

![Image 22: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-10/30/14/asset/4a177c454bb4/sub-buzz-1339-1698675240-1.jpg?crop=1600:1380;0,112)

Republic Records/Big Machine Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.259

**Taylor's Version's biggest difference:** higher loudness

A running theme across _1989 (Taylor’s Version)_ is its loudness compared to the first version. This is easy to hear in “Out of the Woods (Taylor’s Version)” when comparing the chorus’s side-by-side. In Taylor’s Version, the synths are on equal footing with the vocals, as opposed to the first version where the synths are still prominent, but below the vocals.

11 — "State Of Grace (Acoustic Version)"
----------------------------------------

![Image 24: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-07/9/15/asset/ddccda2938a1/sub-buzz-5073-1688915340-1.jpg)

Big Machine Records/Republic Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.261

**Taylor's Version's biggest difference:** higher loudness

Similar to "Forever & Always (Piano Version)," "State Of Grace (Acoustic Version) (Taylor's Version)" is louder, though with a nearly identical acousticness score between both versions. Taylor's voice sounds more full and forward in Taylor's Version.

10 — "Everything Has Changed"
-----------------------------

![Image 26: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-07/9/15/asset/074bc57ece61/sub-buzz-4721-1688915353-1.jpg)

Big Machine Records/Republic Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.262

**Taylor's Version's biggest difference:** higher energy

Taylor's Version has a higher energy score and higher loudness, but lower acousticness.

One example of this is in the second pre-chorus. There are additional instruments in the background (most noticeably a cello), adding more fullness to Taylor's Version.

9 — "I Know Places"
-------------------

![Image 28: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-10/30/14/asset/291411aa44ca/sub-buzz-628-1698675368-1.jpg?crop=1600:1372;0,116)

Republic Records/Big Machine Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.265

**Taylor's Version's biggest difference:** higher valence (more happiness)

I love singing along to Taylor’s songs, but “I Know Places” is one of her most challenging (those high notes in the chorus!). Taylor’s vocals have consistently matured and improved over the years, and she really lets loose in Taylor’s Version (“and WE RUN!”). The data picked up that Taylor’s Version has a "more positive" sound than the first version — I bet she was excited to rerecord this one!

8 — "All Too Well"
------------------

![Image 30: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-07/9/15/asset/60fd0a32234b/sub-buzz-6408-1688915362-1.jpg)

Big Machine Records/Republic Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.274

**Taylor's Version's biggest difference:** lower valence (less happiness)

As one of Taylor's greatest songs, I was especially curious to see how Taylor's Version would differ on this one.

I read a few comments from Swifties who said Taylor's Version sounds like someone reflecting on a sad love story from their past, where the first version sounds more raw and in the moment. I thought that was an interesting analysis to pair with the Spotify data, given the lower valence score of Taylor's Version (0.132 TV vs 0.337).

A song with so much raw emotion is definitely difficult to recapture, and I think Taylor's Version does have a different feel, but with a similar powerful impact.

Do you think Taylor's Version has a more sad vibe than the first version? I'm curious to hear other opinions!

7 — "Superstar"
---------------

![Image 32: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-07/9/15/asset/c616620df98f/sub-buzz-625-1688915376-3.jpg)

Republic Records/Big Machine Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.279

**Taylor's Version's biggest difference:** lower acousticness

As a big fan of the _Fearless Platinum Edition_ tracks, this one felt different to me upon listening to Taylor's Version.

The first version has a gentle, subtleness to it, where Taylor's Version amps up the vocals, and backing instruments. I particularly like the stylistic vocal changes Taylor made, especially on words like "photograph," adding an extra riff.

6 — "Red"
---------

![Image 34: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-01/13/20/asset/d96dc791faed/sub-buzz-10056-1673641034-4.jpg?crop=2948:2247;0,0)

Big Machine Records/Republic Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.291

**Taylor's Version's biggest difference:** lower valence (less happiness)

This song scores relatively similar across all metrics except for valence. The drop is high from 0.641 to 0.408 (TV).

Taylor's Version increases the volume of the drums and bass in the chorus, so my theory is the louder lower frequencies decreases the "musical positiveness." An interesting result for sure!

5 — "White Horse"
-----------------

![Image 36: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-01/13/20/asset/cfc5ce0ccec7/sub-buzz-10198-1673641077-10.jpg)

Republic Records/Big Machine Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.311

**Taylor's Version's biggest difference:** higher energy

When I first heard "White Horse (Taylor's Version)," I did a double take when the chorus came in. The drums hit much harder in Taylor's Version, changing the vibe of the song. While Taylor's Version doesn't quite have the gentleness of the first version, the added energy showed me the song in a new light.

4 — "Girl at Home"
------------------

![Image 38: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-01/13/20/asset/1c3201c7767e/sub-buzz-9295-1673641048-1.jpg?crop=2948:2247;0,0)

Big Machine Records/Republic Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.319

**Taylor's Version's biggest difference:** lower acousticness

This one is a no-brainer. In fact, before seeing the results, this was the song I knew would be close to the top of the list.

The reworked instrumental makes so much sense, and I am a big fan of the deep synths that fill out the background. There's something about them so satisfying to listen to!

3 — "Breathe"
-------------

![Image 40: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-01/13/20/asset/19ffb2c06e44/sub-buzz-6792-1673641086-7.jpg)

Republic Records/Big Machine Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.345

**Taylor's Version's biggest difference:** lower acousticness

Taylor's more mature vocals add a new element to this beautiful song. The best way to describe the difference is the word _more_.

Taylor's Version adds more volume to the main vocal, the guitars/percussion, and Colbie Caillat's harmonies. Listening to Taylor's Version felt like a new experience, in the best way possible.

2 — "Stay Stay Stay"
--------------------

![Image 42: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-01/13/20/asset/d96dc791faed/sub-buzz-10039-1673641058-5.jpg?crop=2942:2247;0,0)

Big Machine Records/Republic Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.356

**Taylor's Version's biggest difference:** lower valence (less happiness)

At first I was surprised that this song had the second highest distance score. However, I can see why when looking at the data.

The first version of "Stay Stay Stay" has one of the highest valence scores across all the songs in the data set (0.928 out of 1). Such a high "musical positiveness" can be difficult to capture in a new recording, but Taylor still does a great job!

1 — "This Love"
---------------

![Image 44: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-10/30/14/asset/242d0eff2713/sub-buzz-622-1698675565-1.jpg?crop=1600:1396;0,104)

Republic Records/Big Machine Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.39

**Taylor's Version's biggest difference:** lower acousticness

I was shocked (in a good way) when I heard “This Love (Taylor’s Version)” for the first time. The synths and arpeggiators in the chorus are more powerful, and the verses sound more delicate. The acoustic guitar is quieter in the intro, in favor of a light and airy synth that fills up the headphones. This continues into the verses, where the ambient sounds take up more space in the mix than the guitar, transforming the song from an acoustic to an ethereal ballad.

Now, here's the 20 pairs that are the most similar to each other (and it's incredible how Taylor was able to replicate these audio qualities _so_ closely):
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

20 — "Shake It Off"
-------------------

![Image 46: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-10/30/14/asset/242d0eff2713/sub-buzz-643-1698675829-1.jpg?crop=1600:1360;0,116)

Republic Records/Big Machine Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.126

Arguably Taylor’s biggest hit, she took great care in recreating the same upbeat vibes. This is seen by the nearly identical "valence" score of 0.92 vs 0.94 (almost the highest score that can be assigned to a song!).

19 — "New Romantics"
--------------------

![Image 48: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-10/30/14/asset/4a177c454bb4/sub-buzz-1371-1698675923-1.jpg?crop=1600:1376;0,112)

Republic Records/Big Machine Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.123

My absolute favorite track in _1989_ is “New Romantics," and Taylor’s Version lived up to my expectations! In my opinion, the production of the chorus is what makes the song soar, and it is a track that will be on repeat.

18 — "I Almost Do"
------------------

![Image 50: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-07/9/15/asset/ddccda2938a1/sub-buzz-5137-1688916096-2.jpg)

Big Machine Records/Republic Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.118

"I Almost Do" wasn't a highly-listened to track of mine when _Red_ first released, so I'm glad Taylor's Version gave me a reason to revisit it.

Taylor's Version sounds very similar to me, and I like how she captured the delicate guitar plucking throughout the song.

17 — "We Are Never Ever Getting Back Together"
----------------------------------------------

![Image 52: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-07/9/15/asset/ddccda2938a1/sub-buzz-5144-1688916075-1.jpg)

Big Machine Records/Republic Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.113

A [fun fact](https://www.buzzfeed.com/dannicaramirez/weird-facts-fs) about this track — it is the only song from all three albums where the biggest difference between the variables is speechiness (the presence of spoken word within the track). It makes sense for this song to have a higher speechiness due to the spoken word section.

It is interesting that Taylor's Version received the higher score (though still close), perhaps indicating a subtle difference in how she recorded the bridge.

The rest of the metrics, especially energy and loudness, look extremely close.

16 — "Tell Me Why"
------------------

![Image 54: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-07/9/15/asset/074bc57ece61/sub-buzz-4773-1688916062-1.jpg)

Republic Records/Big Machine Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.11

The overall metrics on this song are very similar, especially the valence and danceability. I've always loved the background harmonies in the chorus, and they really shine in Taylor's Version.

15 — "Starlight"
----------------

![Image 56: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-07/9/15/asset/4061bcae016c/sub-buzz-410-1688916044-1.jpg)

Big Machine Records/Republic Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.098

What a marvelous tune, indeed! While the energy score for Taylor's Version is slightly lower, the rest of the metrics are so close that the album covers on the graph overlap each other. Very impressive!

14 — "Sad Beautiful Tragic"
---------------------------

![Image 58: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-01/13/20/asset/d07b5a3fde82/sub-buzz-892-1673641310-5.jpg?crop=2929:2247;0,0)

Big Machine Records/Republic Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.097

"Sad Beautiful Tragic" is an underrated track from _Red_. I've always liked how the title of the song perfectly encapsulates the vibe: sad, but beautiful.

Taylor closely captures the high acousticness and low valence score. I find it interesting that Taylor's Version has a slightly lower valence score (0.232 vs. 0.261), (as if it were possible to make it sound even sadder)!

I also thought it was cool that the danceability score was high for this song, likely due to the 3/4 time signature.

13 — "Long Live"
----------------

![Image 60: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-07/9/15/asset/ddccda2938a1/sub-buzz-5130-1688915864-1.jpg)

Scott Legato/TAS23 / Getty Images for TAS Rights Management/Big Machine Records/Republic Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.095

A top ten favorite of mine, I was super excited for Taylor's Version, and it didn't disappoint.

Am I slightly salty that it was performed for the first time so soon after my [Eras tour](https://www.buzzfeed.com/noahblazevic/taylor-swift-era-quiz) show? Maybe. But I'm happy for the millions of Swifties that will get to scream "a band of thieves in ripped-up jeans got to rule the world."

12 — "Sparks Fly"
-----------------

![Image 62: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-07/9/15/asset/60fd0a32234b/sub-buzz-6423-1688915810-13.jpg)

Scott Legato/TAS23 / Getty Images for TAS Rights Management/Big Machine Records/Republic Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.095

Drop everything now! I'll never forget the opening of the Speak Now World Tour (my first arena concert), and the magic of that night.

Taylor's Version hit hard with this one, and every metric is close together, though Taylor's Version is slightly louder.

11 — "Fearless"
---------------

![Image 64: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-01/13/20/asset/35a0f3926130/sub-buzz-9475-1673641285-2.jpg)

Republic Records/Big Machine Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.095

Another top ten favorite of mine, I think Taylor captures the energy and happiness of the first version. This song definitely takes me back to high school, and it is a new perspective hearing it with Taylor's more mature vocals.

10 — "If This Was a Movie"
--------------------------

![Image 66: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-07/9/15/asset/1007dd4722e1/sub-buzz-3563-1688915754-1.jpg)

Republic Records/Big Machine Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.094

I was shook when Taylor rereleased "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)" under _Fearless_ instead of _Speak Now_, allowing for _Speak Now_ to be an album written solely by herself.

Every metric looks very close, with the biggest difference being the lower acousticness of Taylor's Version. The instruments in Taylor's Version do have more of a presence, especially the drums in the second chorus.

9 — "The Lucky One"
-------------------

![Image 68: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-01/13/20/asset/cfc5ce0ccec7/sub-buzz-10214-1673641321-1.jpg?crop=2942:2247;0,0)

Big Machine Records/Republic Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.094

"The Lucky One" is another song that flew under my radar until Taylor's Version, but I now find myself listening to it more often.

Both versions sound similar, but I found a small difference in the drums throughout the song — which have a more rounded and punchy tone in the first version.

8 — "22"
--------

![Image 70: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-01/13/20/asset/d96dc791faed/sub-buzz-10056-1673641331-7.jpg?crop=2942:2247;0,0)

Big Machine Records/Republic Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.093

While Taylor's Version is slightly louder, it still has the low acousticness and high energy, valence, and danceability of the first version.

7 — "Innocent"
--------------

![Image 72: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-07/9/15/asset/ddccda2938a1/sub-buzz-5116-1688915675-1.jpg)

Scott Legato/TAS23 / Getty Images for TAS Rights Management/Big Machine Records/Republic Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.093

I will forever shout from the mountaintops that "Innocent" is one of the three most underrated tracks from _Speak Now_ (the others being "Never Grow Up" and "[Superman](https://www.buzzfeed.com/ravenishak/superman-first-reactions-reviews)").

While the first version has a slightly higher acoustic metric, it is close across the board — especially in the low valence score, which captures the emotion of the music.

6 — "Fifteen"
-------------

![Image 74: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-01/13/20/asset/cfc5ce0ccec7/sub-buzz-10198-1673641293-13.jpg)

Republic Records/Big Machine Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.091

I feel like Taylor took extra time on the instrumental of this song, because it sounds seamless to the first version. Hearing it from the perspective of adult Taylor is so poetic.

5 — "How You Get the Girl"
--------------------------

![Image 76: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-10/30/14/asset/b6036a9ea36b/sub-buzz-1308-1698676086-1.jpg?crop=1600:1388;0,104)

Republic Records/Big Machine Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.078

Another underrated _1989_ track, I hope it gets the attention it deserves with Taylor’s Version. One of my favorite parts of the 1989 World Tour was this song, and the choreography with the umbrellas. It is still a bop almost 10 years later!

4 — "All You Had to Do Was Stay"
--------------------------------

![Image 78: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-10/30/14/asset/ba956eda8a88/sub-buzz-1373-1698676186-1.jpg?crop=1600:1392;0,104)

Republic Records/Big Machine Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.072

This is a track that grew on me over the years, and Taylor perfectly re-created the “stay!” in the background vocals. “All You Had to Do Was Stay” is super fun, and I wonder if it was between this song and “Say Don’t Go” when choosing the track list for the original album.

3 — "Wildest Dreams"
--------------------

![Image 80: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-10/30/14/asset/dbc07ff18cdc/sub-buzz-1570-1698676274-1.jpg?crop=1600:1396;0,104)

Republic Records/Big Machine Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.068

Another top 10 favorite of mine, I was pleasantly surprised to hear how similar Taylor’s Version is to the first version. While Taylor’s Version has a very slightly higher valence (happiness) rating, the production ranks similar across the board. In fact, both versions received the exact same score for loudness!

2 — "Better Than Revenge"
-------------------------

![Image 82: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-07/9/15/asset/ddccda2938a1/sub-buzz-5094-1688915598-1.jpg)

Scott Legato/TAS23 / Getty Images for TAS Rights Management/Big Machine Records/Republic Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.058

The irony that "Better Than Revenge" is the second most similar to its first version —according to this data — is that it contains the lyric change heard around the world.

That aside, I do think Taylor's Version has a similar audio vibe to the first version. Though, the increased volume on the spoken and distorted vocals in the verses gives them an extra level of presence.

1 — "Welcome to [New York](https://www.buzzfeed.com/mychalthompson/tiffany-new-york-pollard-non-binary)"
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

![Image 84: photo of a graph comparing the albums data](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2023-10/30/14/asset/780dfa8276d7/sub-buzz-410-1698676366-1.jpg?crop=1600:1376;0,112)

Republic Records/Big Machine Records/Tidyverse/Andrew Firriolo/BuzzFeed

**Distance:** 0.051

I asked multiple friends which song from _1989 (Taylor’s Version)_ they think sounds the most similar, and quite a few mentioned “Welcome to New York.” Looking at the graph, almost all the points overlap each other completely, showing how she was able to capture each audio quality. This was one of the surprise songs at my Eras Tour show, so it is cool to see it ranked the closest to its first version across all 72 tracks!

After comparing the audio characteristics of the songs, the results I found were thought-provoking! Other factors like lyric, melodic, and vocal changes would be an addition for deeper analysis, though more difficult to quantify.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Which Taylor's Version track do you think has the biggest difference and which is the most similar? Let me know in the comments! Now, back to streaming _1989 (Taylor's Version_)!
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
